https://www.barrons.com/articles/apples-super-cycle-talk-ends-bulls-find-other-things-to-love-1517585057 Apple’s Super Cycle Talk Ends, Bulls Find Other Things to Love By Feb. 2, 2018 10:24 a.m. ET Text Size Medium Large 
Shares of Apple ( AAPL ) are down $3.89, or 2%, at $163.89, trading down with an overall down market, after the company yesterday afternoon beat fiscal Q1 expectations, albeit on lower-than-expected iPhone units , and missed with its outlook for this quarter, as had been widely expected, and said it plans to balance out its cash and debt over time so that it achieves a “neutral,” or zero net balance of cash, plowing money into capital allocations. 
The stock has gotten two downgrades this morning, from Bernstein and from KeyBanc Capital Markets , both cutting the stock to the equivalent of a Hold rating as they assess what to many is shaping up not to be the “super cycle” Wall Street hoped for with the iPhone. 
KeyBanc ’s Andy Hargreaves , cutting the stock to Sector Weight from Overweight, writes that the iPhone results suggest a “saturated market,” including at the high end of the market, and “lower pricing power than we and many investors anticipated.” 
He thinks the “stagnant” iPhone will overshadow Apple’s services business through the next two years. 
He sees capacity for a giant increase in the dividend, but thinks Apple will take a more measured approach: 
We estimate Apple's current net cash balance and projected cash flow could comfortably support a 200%+ increase in the annual dividend by 2020. This could drive stock appreciation by transitioning the stock to trade off of yield, even in a stagnant earnings environment. Despite this opportunity, we believe management will take a more modest approach to the dividend so as not to signal a lack of growth or increase interest rate sensitivity in the shares. So, while a path to significant appreciation through yield is available, we believe a more modest approach is likely. 
For some, the capital returns story is enough, combined with the rising services business 
For example, Shebly Seyrafi with FBN Securities , reiterates an Outperform rating, and raises his price target to $210 from $200, writing that his peers how have downgraded the stock “are wrong." 
Consider the year-ago Q1 had an extra week in it, writes Seyrafi. And the iPhone average selling price surged last quarter to $796. And, there is “much capital return left as Apple targets net cash to eventually go to near zero." 
Others see virtue in Apple’s approach. For example, William Blair’s Arjun Bhatia , reiterating an Outperform rating, writes that the “highly anticipated results provided some vindication for Apple’s pricing strategy as the increase in ASPs more than offset the decline in unit volumes this quarter." 
He concludes “we remain positive on the iPhone longer term as the ever-strengthening Apple ecosystem continues to drive consumers to the iPhone despite the increasing price points." 
Even those slashing estimates for the iPhone see many forces at work for Apple. For example, Canaccord Genuity ’s Mike Walkley , reiterating a Buy rating, and a $200 price target, cuts his iPhone estimates for this year and next to 226 million ad 231 million units, respectively, from 241 million and 239 million. 
However, he also raises his fiscal 2019 profit per share estimate to $12.83, from a prior $12.51 per share, to account for the new tax rate of 15% versus 25% previously. 
The outlook from Apple was lower, but “better than feared,” he writes, and the results for the “Other” category of product, which includes Apple Watch , were “impressive.” 
Plus, sales into China not only were up 11%, but on a weekly basis rose by 19%, on average, citing, again, the shortened number of weeks in the quarter. 
Overall, he sees Apple “continuing to grow its leading market share of the premium-tier smartphone market with double digit growth of its installed base during the quarter." 
Walkley thinks "the iPhone installed base of new iPhone users will exceed 635M exiting C2017,” which is “impressive,” and "should drive strong iPhone replacement sales and earnings, as well as cash flow generation to fund strong long-term capital returns." Most Popular
